q: The quantum-classical gap in query complexity: the decision tree complexity D(f) and quantum query complexity Q(f) are related by the polynomial method. The polynomial method (Beals-Buhrman-Cleve-Mosca-de Wolf) shows:
opts: D(f) = O(Q(f)^6) — any quantum algorithm can be 'dequantized' with at most polynomial overhead
exp: BBCMW polynomial method: Q(f) ≥ deg(f)/2, where deg(f) is the degree of the unique real multilinear polynomial representing f. Also D(f) ≤ Q(f)^6 (Nisan-Szegedy). The gap between Q and D can be at most polynomial, even though constant factors can show exponential quantum speedup.
